text:
**Short answer:** about 200 W of panels refills a 1,000 Wh station in roughly a day and a half of decent sun. For a full recharge in one day, plan on 300-350 W.

**Why the panel's rated watts overstate what you get**
- Panels rarely deliver their label rating. Heat, sun angle, and charge-controller losses leave you about 70-75% of it ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- What counts is peak sun hours, not daylight hours. Most of the US averages about 4-5, summer in the Southwest reaches 6 or more, and northern winters drop to 2-3.
- The formula is: panel watts ≈ 1,000 ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75).

**Panel watts for a one-day full recharge from empty** ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/))

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts needed |
|---|---|
| 3 (cloudy or winter) | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 (good summer day) | ~270 W |
| 6 (Southwest summer) | ~230 W |

In a northern winter with about 2 sun hours, it takes around 735 W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**If you're fine with 1-2 days:** a 200 W panel yields about 630 Wh per day at 4.5 sun hours. That is about 1.5 days to refill, and a 400 W panel takes under a day ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Check these before you buy**
1. **Your station's maximum solar input.** Panels above that wattage add nothing. A 200 W cap means 200 W is all you'll get, no matter the panel size.
2. **Input voltage range.** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's window. Over-voltage can damage the charge controller, and wiring panels in series adds voltage.
3. **Connector type.** Most panels use MC4, while stations often take XT60 or DC barrel plugs, so you may need an adapter.
4. **Power use while charging.** Anything you run during the day reduces the net charge.

**One option if your station accepts 400 W:** the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) has a Voc of 45.3 V, so it suits 12-60 V solar inputs. It's listed at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 ([listing](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)). It weighs 18.5 kg, which is heavy for a folding panel.
